title: PracticePay Patient Financing — Monthly Payment, Interest Charging, AutoPay and Due-Day Rules
content:
This policy of PracticePay Patient Financing governs how each plan's monthly payment is set, how interest is charged, AutoPay, due-day changes and prepayment.

## Monthly payment

- **Payment method clause (no longer in force).** The clause under which each plan's monthly payment follows its payment method as a level payment that repays the financed amount at the plan APR over the term (the monthly rate being the plan APR divided by 1200) for deferred-interest, reduced-APR and standard plans, and as the financed amount divided equally over the term for no-interest plans, is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current terms for a payment reset of a PracticePay plan.
- **Rounding and floor (in force).** Payments are rounded up to the next cent and never below the plan's smallest monthly payment, with the final payment absorbing the difference.
- A deferred-interest plan's payment does not by itself pay the plan off within the promotional period.

## Interest

On reduced-APR and standard plans interest is charged at each statement closing (the plan's statement-closing days before the due date) as simple daily interest at the plan APR on the plan balance excluding fees for the days of the statement period; no-interest plans never charge interest; deferred-interest plans accrue interest only to the memo. Interest is charged only on a plan in active status: a plan that is paid off, cancelled or charged off carries no monthly interest charge.

| Plan type | Interest at each statement closing |
|---|---|
| reduced APR or standard, plan active | simple daily interest at the plan APR on the plan balance excluding fees, for the days of the statement period |
| no interest | none, ever |
| deferred interest | none charged; interest accrues only to the deferred interest memo |

## AutoPay

- **AutoPay clause (no longer in force).** The clause that AutoPay can be turned on or off at any time and carries no rate discount is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current terms for a payment reset of a PracticePay plan.

## Due-day changes

The due day can be changed no more than the plan's due-day changes per plan, to a day from 1 to 28, with the first new due date the first date on the new day later than the current next due date; the payment amount does not change. The count of changes allowed is the per-plan figure in the payment-terms table, and it is read from the plan's own record.

*Hypothetical cases.* With a current next due date of 15 June: a change to the 3rd makes 3 July the first new due date; a change to the 20th makes 20 June the first new due date. A request for the 30th is outside the days 1 to 28 and is not a due day this policy allows.

## Prepayment

There is no prepayment penalty.
